newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on low U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on low U.S. inflation.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Tuesday, boosted by surging U.S. Treasuries after a lower-than-expected U.S. consumer prices report.
"There was some short-covering on the report," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 89-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 124.80.
Despite the uplifting consumer report, however, traders were not convinced the gains would be sustained because the U.S. Federal Reserve could still hike rates in May.
"My impression is that the market's outlook is still not clear," said another trader.
The fact that activity remained very thin Tuesday was testimony to the fact that the market is still uncertain, said traders.
